source: Beyond Horizons API v0.1.0 (deterministic Ares-180 seed)

catalog.name: Enhanced exercise protocol
catalog.description: Prioritized resistive and aerobic exercise scheduling, intended to limit muscle and bone deconditioning across the mission.
limitations: Effect on the simulation's muscle/bone accumulators is modeled qualitatively (faster muscle recovery, slower bone-risk accumulation), not a quantified clinical effect size from a specific study.
Does not fully prevent deconditioning; the simulation still accrues some risk.

catalog.name: Supplemental radiation shielding & monitoring
catalog.description: Additional shielding placement and dosimetry monitoring, intended to slow how quickly radiation burden accumulates over the mission.
limitations: Effect on the simulation's radiation accumulator is modeled qualitatively (a slower accumulation rate), not a quantified shielding-effectiveness figure.
Does not model an acute high-dose event (e.g. a solar particle event) differently.

catalog.name: Sleep & cognitive-load management protocol
catalog.description: Structured sleep scheduling and operational-workload pacing, intended to speed sleep-debt recovery and cognitive-resilience adaptation.
limitations: Effect on the simulation's sleep-recovery and cognitive-adaptation rates is modeled qualitatively, not a quantified clinical effect size.
Cannot fully offset a high-workload day (e.g. an EVA) in the simulation.

counterfactual.disclaimer: Exploratory synthetic simulation; not clinical prediction.
counterfactual.language_note: Exploratory synthetic comparison. Peaks, mean uncertainty and EVA completion probability are heuristic estimates from the simulation engine, not validated predictions or medical guidance.

alternatives.description: Maintain EVA: proceed with the EVA as scheduled on day 145 with the originally assigned crew member.
Delay EVA: postpone the EVA by 10 days (to day 155), same crew member.
Reassign + Recovery: nova performs the EVA on day 145 instead, with a sleep-recovery protocol applied mission-wide.

recommendations.justification: Alternative C maximizes eva_completion_probability - peak_operational_risk (0.360 - 0.531 = -0.171), the mission-success-weighted view of this decision: get the EVA done, with the lowest peak operational risk along the way.
limitations: Utility formula is this project's own operational framing, not a validated decision model.
eva_completion_probability is a bounded heuristic (app/services/counterfactual.py), not a validated prediction.
Does not weigh crew physiological cost on its own terms.

recommendations.justification: Alternative C maximizes -(0.5 * peak_cognitive_risk + 0.5 * peak_musculoskeletal_risk) (-(0.5*0.748 + 0.5*0.594) = -0.671), a crew-health-only view that deliberately ignores mission completion.
limitations: Utility formula is this project's own operational framing, not a validated decision model.
eva_completion_probability is a bounded heuristic (app/services/counterfactual.py), not a validated prediction.
peak_musculoskeletal_risk is itself a reporting-only average (0.5*bone_risk + 0.5*(1-muscle_recovery)), not a value the engine computes directly.

recommendations.justification: Alternative C maximizes eva_completion_probability - mean_uncertainty (0.360 - 0.167 = 0.193), favoring the alternative most likely to yield a completed, usable EVA under the comparison window's shared uncertainty level.
limitations: Utility formula is this project's own operational framing, not a validated decision model.
eva_completion_probability is a bounded heuristic (app/services/counterfactual.py), not a validated prediction.

mean_uncertainty is identical across all three alternatives in this seed (it does not vary with the EVA decision itself), so this role's ranking is driven entirely by eva_completion_probability here -- not evidence that uncertainty is irrelevant in general.

recommendations.justification: Every role recommends alternative C, but C does not win on every metric: alternative B has the better peak_musculoskeletal_risk (0.561 vs C's 0.594). A utility score that aggregates several risk dimensions can hide a dimension where the 'winning' alternative is not actually best -- check the dimension your decision cares about most before treating this consensus as final.
limitations: The skeptic role critiques the other roles' reasoning; it does not run an independent model.
Every comparison here shares the same simulation engine and the same scenario-authoring choices (app/services/counterfactual.py) -- this critique cannot surface a blind spot common to all four roles.

data.evidence_reference: OSD-720 (GLDS-699, cardiac transcriptome, ground-based simulated radiation) and NAG9-1024 (rat skin, ground-based radiation + retinoid countermeasure)
limitations: Ground-based simulated/accelerator radiation, not spaceflight
Cardiac (OSD-720) and skin (NAG9-1024) tissue only; not verified for other tissues
Animal models (mouse, rat), not human

data.evidence_reference: HRP-RADIATION-CARCINOGENESIS: NASA formally tracks a Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis from cumulative mission exposure
limitations: The source page tracks this as a long-term, population-level risk category, not a per-individual diagnosis, timeline or specific gene/mutation this project can honestly report for a given crew member

This project has no data linking a specific dose in the simulation to a quantified change in cancer probability -- the weight above is a qualitative scenario parameter, not a dose-response figure from the source

data.evidence_reference: Scenario hypothesis, informed by HRP-BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH gap BMed-102 (radiation/CNS effects on cognition, an open research gap per that page, largely animal-studied)
limitations: Human evidence for radiation's cognitive effects is limited (an open gap per the source page)
Not independently verified against a specific dataset in this project

data.evidence_reference: NAG9-1024: radiation altered stress-response, immune/inflammation and DNA-repair gene expression in irradiated rat skin
limitations: Rat skin, ground-based accelerator radiation only
Association observed in gene expression data, not a demonstrated mechanism in humans

data.evidence_reference: HRP-BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH: risk page cites sleep/performance studies (gap BMed-101)
limitations: Official NASA risk-page summary, not a specific quantitative effect size
Individual variability in sleep resilience is not modelled here

data.evidence_reference: HRP-BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH: risk statement links cognitive/behavioral stressors to in-mission performance
limitations: General risk framing from the official risk page, not a specific dose-response curve

data.evidence_reference: Scenario hypothesis; the individual links (sleep->cognitive load, cognitive load->cognitive performance risk) are each supported_evidence above, but this specific downstream link to operational error is not independently verified
limitations: Chained from two supported_evidence edges but not itself independently verified
No specific verified NASA source connecting cognitive performance risk directly to error rates

data.evidence_reference: AINV0000000837: Hughes-Fulford osteoblast microgravity gene-expression data (Shuttle Biorack, STS-76/81/84), backed by 4 peer-reviewed papers
limitations: Cell culture (MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts), not intact bone or a whole organism
Short spaceflight exposure (hours), not a multi-month mission

data.evidence_reference: HRP-BONE-RISK: NASA reference page and 2017/2024 evidence reports (NTRS 20170004597, 20240005190) -- astronauts lose 1-1.5% of bone density per month during 4-6 month missions
limitations: Population-level astronaut DXA-scan data, not the specific Ares-180 crew
The source itself says it is unclear whether bone density stabilises or keeps declining on missions longer than 4-6 months (Ares-180 is 180 days)

data.evidence_reference: HRP-MUSCLE-RISK: NASA reference page -- ISS crew who adhere to the exercise schedule with adequate countermeasure equipment return with only minimal losses of muscle size, strength and endurance
limitations: The 'minimal losses' finding is tied to ISS-era exercise hardware; the source itself flags that exploration-mission hardware may not have the same capability
No specific quantitative effect size is given (this engine's rate constants remain synthetic_parameter)

data.evidence_reference: Scenario hypothesis linking physical deconditioning to operational error
limitations: No specific verified NASA source connecting muscle deconditioning directly to error rates

data.evidence_reference: HRP-EVA-RISK: NASA formally tracks a Risk of Mission Impacting Injury and Compromised Performance due to EVA Operations
limitations: The source page itself states that injury mechanisms and individual risk factors (sex, anthropometry, fitness) are not yet understood -- this edge claims only that EVA carries a recognized risk, not a specific mechanism or effect size
Planetary (non-microgravity) EVA physiological demands are characterised only for a limited number of Lunar/Mars analogue sites per the source

data.evidence_reference: Scenario hypothesis based on general EVA physical-demand framing
limitations: HRP-EVA-RISK (verified) covers injury/performance risk broadly, not specifically EVA's effect on muscle-recovery capacity
No specific verified NASA source ties EVA load directly to muscle-recovery decline

genes.study_citation: Burns FJ, Chen S, Xu G, Wu F, Tang MS (2002). The Action of a Dietary Retinoid on Gene Expression and Cancer Induction in Electron-irradiated Rat Skin. J Radiat Res 43(Suppl):S229-S232.
genes.radiation_condition: 9 Gy or 18 Gy electron irradiation, with/without a 300 ppm dietary retinyl acetate (vitamin A) supplement
limitations: Rat skin, not human or astronaut tissue.
Ground-based electron irradiation (ground accelerator), not spaceflight radiation.
Single timepoint (24 hours post-exposure) -- not a trajectory over a mission.
Gene expression change (how much a gene's activity went up or down), not a mutation -- this study did not sequence DNA for mutations, and this project has no mutation-level data for any gene.
8740 genes were on the array; these are the ones the paper itself highlighted as most strongly altered -- not an exhaustive list of every gene radiation affects.

rankings.language_note: These are this project's own hypothetical experiment proposals, built from gaps visible in the evidence graph (GET /api/v1/evidence/graph). They are not funded, scheduled, or endorsed by NASA -- see each proposal's limitations.

proposals.title: Radiation + Sleep + Cognition
proposals.gap_description: The evidence graph links radiation exposure and sleep debt to cognitive resilience only through exploratory_hypothesis edges (app/domain/evidence_graph.py) -- no dataset in this project's registry (app/core/evidence_registry.py) measures the combined effect of radiation dose and sleep debt on cognition in the same subjects. The closest real source on file (JSC, DOI 10.83263/2p33-rp27) covers sleep medication and abrupt-awakening cognition, but not radiation.
limitations: Hypothetical experiment design, not a funded or scheduled NASA study.
Impact, uncertainty and information-gain scores are this project's own qualitative judgment calls, not measured quantities.
Would require a combined radiation + sleep-restriction ground analog; no such combined protocol exists among this project's verified sources.

proposals.title: Isolation + Circadian Rhythm + Performance
proposals.gap_description: The evidence graph's behavioral-health edges (backed by HRP-BEHAVIORAL-HEALTH) cover isolation and confinement broadly, but not the specific interaction between circadian misalignment and operational performance -- this remains an exploratory_hypothesis edge with no dedicated dataset.
limitations: Hypothetical experiment design, not a funded or scheduled NASA study.
Impact, uncertainty and information-gain scores are this project's own qualitative judgment calls, not measured quantities.
Isolation effects are highly context-dependent (crew size, mission phase, communication delay); a ground analog may not transfer cleanly to flight.

proposals.title: Microgravity + Muscle + Bone
proposals.gap_description: Bone and muscle loss are each backed by real sources individually (the Hughes-Fulford osteoblast dataset and the HRP bone/muscle risk pages), but no single dataset measures bone and muscle decline together under microgravity in the same crew member over time -- musculoskeletal_risk in the simulation engine is a reporting-only heuristic, not a value read from data.
limitations: Hypothetical experiment design, not a funded or scheduled NASA study.
Impact, uncertainty and information-gain scores are this project's own qualitative judgment calls, not measured quantities.
A combined longitudinal bone+muscle dataset under long-duration microgravity is costlier (longer duration, more instrumentation) than the other two proposals, reflected in its higher relative_cost.
